 LIVE Updated 1 min ago Arsenal vs Everton LIVE - score, Ezri Konsa goal, commentary stream
 Live coverage of the Arsenal vs Everton Premier League clash from the Emirates Stadium
 It's Arsenal vs Everton today 
 Add to preferred sources Comments Sport Paul Wheelock Head of sport and Christopher Beesley Everton reporter Updated 15:29, 24 Oct 2026 Welcome to our live coverage of Everton's Premier League match against Arsenal. The Blues are trailing 1-0 to Ezri Konsa's seventh-minute opener.
 Everton have headed to the home of the defending champions on the back of their first defeat of the season. They went down 2-0 at home to Chelsea last weekend to end their eight-match unbeaten run in all competitions.
 And they are going to need to produce an excellent performance to take anything from an Arsenal side who have won 10 of the 12 games they have played in the current campaign.
 And with manager David Moyes without Jarrad Branthwaite and Jack Grealish , their task has become even tougher. That said, they did run the Gunners close in last season's corresponding clash, which they lost harshly 2-0 late on.
 So can the Blues improve on that result today? We've got Chris Beesley at the Emirates Stadium and Paul Wheelock back on Merseyside to bring you an in-game commentary stream and the best post-match reaction and analysis.
 ‌ 
 New Updates Key Events
 GOAL: Arsenal 1-0 Everton (Konsa) View Post Reasons for Branthwaite and Grealish absences View Post Arsenal line-up confirmed View Post Everton team confirmed View Post Today 15:29 BST Wide of the target
 Noni Maduke fashions a chance for Arsenal having got the better of Vitalii Mykolenko. Jordan Pickford will feel he had it covered as the subsequent shot flies wide.
 Comments Paul Wheelock Today 15:25 BST Former Liverpool man impressed
 Stephen Warnock, the former Liverpool defender, is watching the game for Final Score and he's just said: "Their response has brilliant, at the start of the game they allowed Arsenal to come onto them. But Everton are back in this game in terms of confidence."
 Comments Paul Wheelock Today 15:23 BST Everton need to show more conviction
 So, we're midway thorugh the first half and while Everton aren't out of this contest, they're finding themselves second best to the champions in the rain. The Blues have had their moments but need to show a bit more conviction.
 Comments Chris Beesley Today 15:22 BST Timely by Rohl
 Noni Madueke just hung a floating cross into the Everton area towards Gyokores but Merlin Rohl was on hand to cut it out with an acrobatic clearance. The result is another Arsenal corner though.
 Comments Chris Beesley Today 15:19 BST Ball won't drop for Blues
 I've just been watching a replay of Dewsbury-Hall's corner and unlike the one from which Arsenal took the lead, the ball wouldn't drop kindly for Everton in the area.
 Mikel Merino almost knocked it into his own goal but Gabriel was on hand on the goal-line to hack it clear.
 Comments Chris Beesley Today 15:17 BST George denied
 Everton try and build an attack down the left through Tyrique George and Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall but the latter gets bundled off the ball. One thing is for sure, the Blues can't sit back like they did in the corresponding fixture last season - although they still had some good chances that day before the hosts broke the deadlock.
 Now George has a shot which is deflected wide off Ben White's boot.
 Comments Chris Beesley Today 15:12 BST Garner tests Raya
 Everton's first chance of significance as they patienctly build up an opportunity for Garner to drill in a low shot. David Raya struggled to keep hold of the ball on this wet surface and Harrison Armstrong was ready to pounce on the rebound but the Spanish keeper managed to cling on in the end.
 Comments Chris Beesley Today 15:09 BST Sloppy from Everton
 Pickford and Armstrong both went for the same ball as it bounced off the crossbar from Gyokores' effort, Mykolenko couldn't clear the danger and Knosa pounced. Arsenal seem to have mastered such goals from set-pieces but it's hardly high level stuff.
 David Moyes, now wearing a cap in the rain, doesn't seem impressed though. It was sloppy defending from his side and just the kind of start they wanted to avoid.
 Comments Chris Beesley Today 15:07 BST GOAL: Arsenal 1-0 Everton (Konsa)
 There's some penalty box pinball from Odergaard's corner and Konsa bundles the ball in from close range.
 Comments Chris Beesley Today 15:05 BST O'Brien to the rescue
 Now Eze escapes down the left wing and pulls back a low cross to Gyokeres but Jake O'Brien puts it out for a corner.
 Comments Chris Beesley Today 15:04 BST Mykolenko block
 Some early defending to do for Vitalii Mykolenko as he makes a crucial block on a Declan Rice shot.
 Comments Chris Beesley Today 15:04 BST Everton have to 'dig in'
 That's the verdict of former Everton winger Pat Nevin, speaking on BBC Radio 5 Live:
 The expectation is that Arsenal are massive favourites but Everton have to dig in and look at how arguably the front three for Arsenal are the reserve front three. But they have got very talented players up there. Comments Paul Wheelock Today 15:02 BST High-tempo start
 There's zip on the turf and it's a high-tempo start with Everton's players getting a few early touches as Arsenal press them.
 Comments Chris Beesley Today 15:00 BST Kick-off
 Everton's James Garner gets us underway.
 Comments Chris Beesley Today 14:58 BST Ken Friar remembered
 Ken Friar, who rose from stadium messenger boy to life president at Arsenal, serving the club for eight decades, is being remembered before kick-off with a video about him being shown before kick-off.
 Comments Chris Beesley Today 14:55 BST The teams are here
 Both sets of players are out on the pitch. First we have the Premier League anthem and then the cheery tune that is north London forever.
 Comments Chris Beesley Today 14:51 BST Tuchel in the house
 England manager Thomas Tuchel is present at the Emirates Stadium today.
 It feels like James Tarkowski's international ship has sailed and there is no Jarrad Branthwaite to impress him after featuring in the last set of Three Lions matches.
 Jordan Pickford's form of course will be carefully monitored while James Garner and Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall will both be keen to impress, along with youngsters Harrison Armstrong and Tyrique George.
 Comments Chris Beesley Today 14:40 BST Garner and Armstrong get their eye in
 Everton's players have just beendoing warm-up drills, shooting at third-choice keeper Tom King who is among the substitutes today.
 Both James Garner and Harrison Armstrong are among the scorers. Blues boss David Moyes repeated yesterday how he wants the teenage home-grown hero, who is yet to register at senior level, to add some goals to his game.
 Comments Chris Beesley Today 14:27 BST Kevin Campbell's family welcomed
 A mural by Itaewon of the late Arsenal and Everton striker Kevin Campbell has been put up in Brixton, London, celebrating his life. (Image: Tom Canton & The Kevin Campbell Foundation) 
 Today's matchday programme says:
 We are honoured - and we're sure that Everton supporters will also be delighted - that the family of Kevin Campbell are in attendance today as special guests of the club... Since his passing in June 2024 at the age of 54, his family have established the Kevin Campbell Foundation, which delivers football-based programmes in partnership with both Arsenal and Everton to help young people develop skills, gain confidence and find new opportunities. Comments Chris Beesley Today 14:25 BST Applause at City game finishes
 There's a hearty round of applause from members of the Arsenal fanbase here as screens around the Emirates Stadium show that Aston Villa - managed by former Gunners boss Unai Emery - have defeated title rivals Manchester City 2-1 in today's early Premier League kick-off.
 Comments Chris Beesley Today 14:25 BST Arsenal motivation
 Aston Villa have beaten Manchester City 2-1. It ends the Premier League leaders' 100% winning start.
 And it means should Arsenal defeat Everton today, they woud move level on points with City at the top.
 Improving Villa, meanwhile, move above the Blues into sixth.
 Comments Paul Wheelock Today 14:20 BST Wet one
 I've taken my seat in the press box and can confirm it's very much a wet one here. Jordan Pickford was already out warming up with the other goalkeepers but some of the outfield members of the Everton squad have now joined them. Still no sign of the Arsenal players.
 Comments Chris Beesley Today 14:10 BST Villa leading again
 He's just gone off but Nicolas Jackson earlier scored his second to put Aston Villa 2-1 up against Manchester City. He's a striker I'd always liked to have seen at Everton.
 Comments Paul Wheelock Today 14:05 BST George's big chance
 Three changes for Everton of course and two of those are enforced. Jack Grealish's absence through sickness ensures that Londoner Tyrique George, who previously plied his trade across the capital with Chelsea gets a chance to start against the Premier League champions. Personally, I think he's been unfortunate to lose his place in the side and I would have even liked to have seen him lining up on the opposite flank when Grealish was fit.
 Comments Chris Beesley Today 13:52 BST Reasons for Branthwaite and Grealish absences
 As Chris Beesley reavaled moments ago, Jarrad Branthwaite is absent due to concussion protocols, while Everton have just confirmed that Jack Grealish misses out due to sickness.
 Comments Paul Wheelock Today 13:51 BST Arsenal line-up confirmed
 And here's the Arsenal side...
 Content cannot be displayed without consent Comments Chris Beesley Today 13:46 BST Everton team confirmed
 So, three changes for Everton with Jarrad Branthwaite, Jack Grealish and Ainsley Maitland-Niles dropping out of the side.
 I understand that Branthwaite, who manager David Moyes was tight-lipped about in yesterday's pre-match press conference after not appearing in training footage put out by the club, has NOT suffered a new injury but rather is unavailable due to concussion procedure.
 Everton starting line-up: Pickford; Rohl, Tarkowski, O'Brien; Mykolenko; Garner, Armstrong; Johnson, Dewsbury-Hall, George; Barry. 
 Comments Chris Beesley Today 13:42 BST All square at Villa Park
 And you'll never have guessed who has brought Manchester City level? Erling Haaland, of course. And it came from a brilliant Iliman Ndiaye assist.
 Watching that, and the way Ndiaye took the game to Paris Saint-Germain recently after coming off the bench, was a real reminder of the talent Everton have lost.
 Comments Paul Wheelock Today 13:38 BST Moyes' "monster"
 David Moyes has hailed captain James Tarkowski as Everton’s “anchor” who “trains like a monster every day.”
 The Blues boss said:
 I think Tarky has been a wee bit of a mainstay of the team. He’s been a little bit an anchor in the team and kept us all solid. By the way, up until, I think up until Hull game we had the best clean sheet record, which, in the main, we have been over the last season as well. “So, there’s not really been a huge appetite for me to think about anything other than to keep Tarky doing the job he’s doing. I tell you what, he trains like a monster every day. He tries to make himself the best he can. He’s a big leader round the place as well. Click here for the full story
 Comments Chris Beesley Today 13:29 BST Moyes on Mikel 
 David Moyes is the manager who first brought Mikel Arteta to English football. But he admits he’s not sure how much of his influence has rubbed off on Arsenal’s Premier League-winning boss ahead of Everton’s trip to face them at the Emirates Stadium:
 I always look and I think: ‘Mikel has had Pep, what would he take from me?’ I don’t really know. But I think he might take from me a little bit of the other side. I know how Pep works, how good his teams are and what he’s seen. He’s worked under Pep and he’s seen an awful lot of stuff there. But there’s a lot of other stuff like having a winning culture and a winning team, how you’re dealing with the players, what you’re demanding of them, the standards you set. I hope that in some way he might have taken bits of that. Comments Paul Wheelock Load more entries Follow Liverpool Echo: Facebook
